grh_3cab23f0853f68ec93ac.title: Apartment for Peggy
paragraphs: Retired professor Henry Barnes, convinced that age has made him useless, rents his attic to veteran student Jason Taylor and Jason's energetic pregnant wife Peggy during the postwar housing shortage. Peggy draws Barnes back into life, persuading him to organize classes for veterans' wives and reminding him that knowledge matters only when it helps people. After Peggy loses her baby, guilt and financial pressure drive Jason to abandon school for a better-paying sales job, and Peggy prepares to leave as well. Believing he has lost the people who gave him purpose, Barnes takes what he thinks are sleeping pills, only for Peggy and the returning Jason to discover the tablets were harmless. Jason chooses teaching again, Peggy stays, and Barnes realizes he is needed after all.

This [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]] broadcast aired on September 2, 1949. It is listed as episode 32 in the archive. [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jeanne Crain, Herb Butterfield, George Seaton, Ken Christy, and William Tracy. Other credited names include Bill Cairn as director, Howard Wiley as producer, Faith Baldwin as writer, Warren Lewis as radio adaptor, and Jimmy Wallington as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.4e71d2ba39e366d0|Pabst Beer]].
This version presents a radio version of [[work|work.sdp.film.0c6f07e151baf45c|Apartment for Peggy]]. Warren Lewis adapted it for radio.

grh_3cd472409acc67cca273.title: A Very Nice Couple
paragraphs: Steve Montgomery's endless succession of hobbies and half-started careers strains his marriage to successful radio performer Connie, especially after he drags home a huge piece of granite and announces that he is becoming a sculptor. As Connie spends more time with an admirer and Steve moves from one new pursuit to another, the couple separates and Steve is left miserable. Then a magazine representative looking for Steve's photography sees the untouched granite and mistakes it for striking surrealist sculpture, offering thousands of dollars for it as well as a steady staff photography job. Connie returns with the news, and Steve cares far more about having his wife back than about his accidental artistic success.
